title: generate-icons.ps1 overwrites the social card that generate-social-card.js owns
test: tests/brandScripts.test.js: 'generate-icons.ps1 does not write the social card', 'both brand scripts document that generate-icons.ps1 runs before generate-social-card.js'
proof: On the unchanged code, 'generate-icons.ps1 does not write the social card' failed: scripts/generate-icons.ps1 contained the $heroSocial composition (New-ComposedLogo ... -UseBackground) and Save-Png to nextra-social-card.png, so the source included 'nextra-social-card'. The second test failed because neither script documented the order. After the fix, generate-icons.ps1 no longer composes or saves the card (the -UseBackground parameter stays in New-ComposedLogo, unused by this script), and both script headers document ownership and the run order (generate-icons.ps1 before generate-social-card.js whenever nextra-primary-logo.png changes). Both tests pass. The committed PNG was not regenerated. The PowerShell script parses with 0 errors; it was not executed.
